title: Focus for the CSM
tagline: One ranked list that tells a CSM who needs them today, and why.
summary: An internal workspace for YourDOST Customer Success Managers. It turns 22 accounts into a short, ranked 'needs attention today' list, explains why each account is there, and lets the CSM act and clear it in under a minute.

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: Today view, account detail, log call, handled, not relevant, empty and stale states

stats.label: states designed, from busy to all clear

sections.title: Background
text: YourDOST supports the wellbeing of people in corporates and colleges. Behind every client account is a Customer Success Manager, the CSM, who keeps the account healthy: campaigns running on time, reports delivered, risks caught early and promises kept.

A single CSM looks after many accounts at once. In this concept the user, Sana, has 22. This case study focuses on one problem, seen from the CSM's side: the internal tool they open first thing each morning.

sections.title: Challenge
text: How might we tell a CSM, within seconds of opening the tool, which few accounts need them today and why, and let them act without leaving the page?
The tool should feel like a short, finishable to-do list for the day, not a database they have to dig through.

sections.title: The Problem
text: Account data was there, but nothing was prioritising it for the person responsible. These are the gaps I designed around.

bullets.title: Too many accounts, no starting point
bullets.text: With 22 accounts, a CSM has to decide for themselves where to begin. Quiet-but-risky accounts are easy to miss next to loud, routine ones.

bullets.title: No reason attached to a flag
bullets.text: A red mark without a why makes a CSM open each account to find out. Time is lost before any work starts.

bullets.title: Logging a call feels like admin
bullets.text: If recording an outcome takes a long form, it gets skipped, and the next person sees stale history.

bullets.title: No sense of being done
bullets.text: A list that never shrinks gives no feeling of progress, so the day ends without anyone knowing what is left.

sections.title: Impact
text: What the design is built to change, before it is tested with real CSMs:

bullets.title: A faster start to the day
bullets.text: The Today view opens on a ranked 'Needs attention today' list, ordered by urgency and then impact.

bullets.title: Decisions with context
bullets.text: Every row carries a one-line reason and the numbers behind it, such as 'Engagement −34% · 2 flags · last contact 12d'.

bullets.title: Logging that gets done
bullets.text: Log call is a small dialog with three outcome choices, a note and a next follow-up, and saving marks the account handled.

bullets.title: Visible progress
bullets.text: A 'Handled today: 0 of 6' counter and a Handled group give the CSM a clear end point.

bullets.title: Rank first, then group
bullets.text: The list is ranked by urgency, then impact, and split into Act now and Today. The 9 low-urgency accounts collapse into 'Watching (9) · nothing urgent' so they stay available but out of the way.

bullets.title: Say why in plain words
bullets.text: Each row has a short reason, for example 'You promised a call-back yesterday and it is still open', plus a status chip such as Follow-up, Dropping, Report due or Low sign-ups.

bullets.title: Keep the portfolio picture in view
bullets.text: A side column shows overall engagement for the 22 accounts (68.4%, up 3.1 points, with 9 accounts falling), the follow-ups due and the live campaigns, so the list never loses context.

bullets.title: An account page that explains itself
bullets.text: Opening an account shows 'Why it is here' as a short timeline of signals, an eight-week engagement trend, key context and a single Suggested next step: 'Call the HR lead before noon'.

bullets.title: Act without leaving
bullets.text: Log call, Schedule follow-up and Send nudge sit at the top of the page, and the account panel carries a primary action and a quiet 'Not relevant' option.

bullets.title: A call log under a minute
bullets.text: The dialog says 'Takes under a minute. Saving marks this account handled today.' Outcome is one tap (Reached them, Left voicemail, No answer), and the next follow-up is a tap too: None, Tomorrow, In 3 days or Next week.

bullets.title: Handled is reversible
bullets.text: A handled account moves to 'Handled today' with its outcome, for example 'Reached them · follow-up Tue', and an Undo link beside it. The new follow-up appears in the side column straight away.

bullets.title: Not relevant teaches the ranking
bullets.text: Dismissing an account asks for a reason: Already handled, Expected (nothing to do), Not my account or Other. The dialog says this helps tune the ranking.

bullets.title: Honest empty and stale states
bullets.text: When the list is cleared, the page says 'All clear for today' and keeps the handled items for review. When data is old, a banner says 'This list may be out of date', gives the time of the last sync and promises a refresh when data arrives.

sections.title: Hi-Fi Design: Scan the ranked list
text: The Today view is the CSM's home. A greeting and three quick actions sit above the list. Three counts (Act now, Follow-ups due, Watching) summarise the day, and 'Handled today: 0 of 6' tracks progress.
Filters for All, Corporate and College let a CSM focus on one type of client. The right-hand column keeps engagement, follow-ups and live campaigns in view.
captions: Today view: ranked accounts, reasons and portfolio context

sections.title: Hi-Fi Design: Open an account
text: Selecting Northwind Corp opens its panel in place. 'Why it is here' lists the signals in order: an employee escalation risk flag today, a second flag on Monday, 12 days with no contact and three weeks of declining engagement.
Below it, a trend chart and a small context block (last contact, open follow-ups, live campaign, renewal in 74 days) lead to the suggested next step.
captions: Account detail: why it is here, trend, context and next step

sections.title: Hi-Fi Design: Log the call
text: Choosing Log call opens a compact dialog titled with the account's name. Outcome, a short note ('What was agreed?') and the next follow-up are the only fields, and the primary button reads 'Save and mark handled', so the result of saving is clear before it is pressed.
captions: Log call dialog with outcome, note and next follow-up

sections.title: Hi-Fi Design: Handled, with undo
text: After saving, Northwind Corp leaves the Act now list and appears under 'Handled today (1)' with 'Reached them · follow-up Tue' and an Undo link. The counters update (Today 2, Handled 1 of 6), and the Tuesday follow-up shows up in the side column. A confirmation message at the bottom offers Undo again.
captions: Handled state: the account moves down, counters update, Undo stays close

sections.title: Hi-Fi Design: Not relevant, with a reason
text: If an account should not be on the list, the CSM can say so. A small dialog asks 'Why is Northwind Corp not relevant?' and offers four reasons. The dialog notes that the answer helps tune the ranking, so dismissing becomes feedback and not just a way to hide a row.
captions: Not relevant dialog with four reasons

sections.title: Hi-Fi Design: All clear and stale data
text: Two edge states keep the tool trustworthy. When all six are done, the list is replaced with 'All clear for today', the counters read 0 and 'Handled today: 6 of 6', and every handled account keeps an Undo.

When data has not synced, a banner above the list says it may be out of date and that the last sync was 2 days ago. The ranking stays visible, labelled 'as of then', so the CSM can still work and knows what to trust.
captions: All clear: nothing left, everything reviewable
Stale data: a plain banner above the same list

sections.title: Outcome
text: The result is a daily workspace built around one question, 'Who needs me today, and why?' It reduces 22 accounts to a short, ranked list, explains each flag in a sentence, lets a CSM log the result of a call in a few taps, and gives them a clear point at which they are done.
This is a design concept. It has not been tested with CSMs or measured in use, so the case study describes what the design is intended to do, not results.

bullets.title: Test with real CSMs
bullets.text: Watch a few CSMs start their morning with it. Check whether the ranking matches their own judgement, and where they hesitate.

bullets.title: Make the ranking explainable
bullets.text: Let a CSM see what moved an account up the list, and use the 'Not relevant' reasons to improve it.

bullets.title: Colour-independent states
bullets.text: Make sure risk, follow-up and handled states also read through icons and labels, not only colour.

bullets.title: Handover and shared accounts
bullets.text: Support accounts that change CSM, with Handover notes carried into the same account panel.
